In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) the number, size, and histological features, of granulomas are influenced by the time between the 1st and 2nd exposures to S. schistosomiasis; 2) the level of the primo-infection is a determining factor in the development of the 2nd exposure to S. schisto-somiasis.
the protective immunity is not only dependent upon the number of parasites of the first infection but also on the level of their antigenicity.

(1) the time interval between primo- and secundary infections is of major importance for the evolution of granulomas and the development of immunity; (2) a 6 months period of latency is sufficient to induce a protection against the challenge, but this protection is effective only when the primo-infection is sufficiently high; (3) the rate of primo- and secudary infections is of importance for the evolution and the development of hepatic granuloma and immunity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of antigenic stimulation of the host by primo-infection is a decisive factor for the development of protective immunity against a subsequent infection.
the protective immunity is a result of an interaction between the level of antigenicity and the time of the challenge.
the protective effect against a challenge is obtained in a 6 months interval after a primary infection with S. manson, if the rate of primo-infected cercariae is higher than 50.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of primo-infection plays a role in the stimulation of protective immunity against a subsequent infection.
the rate of primo infection is the most important factor in inducing a protective immunity.
the level of primo-infection is the main factor which determines the degree of protection.
